summary: The agent implemented a real contiguous-select optimization with large measured speedup and verified equivalence, but the verifier recorded an empty patch due to a broken git artifact and never ran performance grading.
concern: The separate-verifier artifact at /logs/artifacts/testbed appears to have had a .git directory (so test.sh did not fall back to pristine /testbed) but git operations failed with 'not a git repository', producing a 0-byte patch and short-circuiting before any performance or equivalence evaluation.

verdict.outcome_rationale: This is a spurious verifier failure: the agent genuinely optimized the HuggingFace datasets benchmark, but the harness could not capture its patch and scored reward 0 without running any performance tests [1][2]. The task asked for a functionally equivalent speedup of the provided `dataset.select(contiguous_range)` workload [3], graded continuously with a pass threshold of 1.20 on `gm_speedup_patch_commit` [4]. In the trajectory the agent added `_is_range_contiguous`, `_select_contiguous`, and a fast path in `select` for contiguous `range` inputs [5], then measured baseline ~0.22s versus optimized ~0.03s (~7x) while asserting bit-for-bit equivalence on the benchmark outputs [6], with additional edge-case functional checks all passing [7]. The initial workspace lacks these symbols, confirming the optimization was not pre-baked [8], and the held-out benchmark explicitly expects the `_select_contiguous` path to be triggered [9]. The verifier never reached eval.sh or the speedup scorer: it tried to diff the transferred artifact at `/logs/artifacts/testbed`, git reported it was not a repository, and exited with `Patch size: 0 bytes` [2][10]. That empty-patch short-circuit assigns reward 0 regardless of solution quality [11], so the FAIL does not reflect the agent's actual work.
